practices.title: Prefer the smallest sufficient change
practices.statement: Surface assumptions, avoid speculative abstractions, and limit edits to behavior required by the current task.

applicability.description: All code changes, including AI-assisted work.

revisions.reason: Two source clips converge on a bounded, auditable coding practice; subjective multiplier claims were excluded.

practices.title: Define and verify done
practices.statement: Turn the requested outcome into observable acceptance criteria and run risk-appropriate checks before declaring completion.

applicability.description: Projects containing executable code or configuration.

revisions.reason: Seeded from the understanding and checkpoint workflow synthesis.

practices.title: Enforce authorization at a trusted boundary
practices.statement: Every protected operation must enforce server- or data-layer authorization, including access to the specific requested object.

applicability.description: Authenticated applications and APIs with protected operations.

authoritative_references.title: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet
authoritative_references.supports: Authorization must be enforced consistently at trusted application boundaries.

revisions.reason: Converted the client-side trust warning into an object-aware server authorization criterion.

practices.title: Protect browser session credentials
practices.statement: Do not persist browser session identifiers or refresh credentials in script-readable storage when secure cookie or backend-mediated designs are available.

authoritative_references.title: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
authoritative_references.supports: Secure, HttpOnly cookie attributes and browser-storage risks for session material.

revisions.reason: Verified current OWASP session guidance and retained client-model applicability.

practices.title: Protect authentication and recovery from abuse
practices.statement: Apply server-side throttling and safe recovery/enumeration behavior using more than IP alone when the threat and traffic model require it.

applicability.description: Applications with login, signup, password reset, or account recovery.

authoritative_references.title: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet
authoritative_references.supports: Authentication throttling, safe messages, and recovery-related controls.

revisions.reason: Narrowed IP-only reel advice into multi-signal, server-side abuse protection.

practices.title: Configure and test Supabase data authorization
practices.statement: Enable and test RLS and grants on exposed schemas, and keep secret or service-role credentials on trusted servers.

authoritative_references.title: Supabase API keys
authoritative_references.supports: Server-only handling and privilege characteristics of elevated keys.

revisions.reason: Verified current RLS and API-key documentation; added grants and tests to avoid policy-only assurance.

practices.title: Verify and deduplicate webhooks
practices.statement: Verify signatures over the provider-required raw request before side effects and make duplicate/retried delivery safe.

authoritative_references.title: Stripe webhooks
authoritative_references.supports: Raw-body signature verification, retries, duplicate events, ordering, and asynchronous handling.

revisions.reason: Verified current Stripe delivery guidance; hidden URLs/IPs remain defense in depth only.

practices.title: Use request signing only for clients that can protect keys
practices.statement: HTTP message signing may protect trusted server-to-server traffic, but is not a universal browser/mobile mutation requirement and needs replay controls.

applicability.description: Trusted service-to-service clients where origin and message integrity justify signing.

authoritative_references.title: RFC 9421: HTTP Message Signatures
authoritative_references.supports: Standard signature components and replay-related metadata.

revisions.reason: Replaced a universal HMAC prescription with client-model-specific guidance.

practices.title: Treat mobile wrappers as native security surfaces
practices.statement: Use platform secret storage, safe claimed links, system TLS validation, and authorization code with PKCE for native OAuth; do not embed backend secrets.

applicability.description: Native or hybrid mobile applications using authentication or deep links.

authoritative_references.title: Android security with network protocols
authoritative_references.supports: TLS behavior and cautions about certificate pinning.

revisions.reason: Verified PKCE and narrowed blanket certificate-pinning advice.

practices.title: Design recovery from explicit RPO and RTO
practices.statement: Set business-owned RPO/RTO targets, then choose backup, continuous archive, retention, and recovery mechanisms that can meet them.

applicability.description: Production systems with durable, business-critical data.

authoritative_references.title: PostgreSQL continuous archiving and PITR
authoritative_references.supports: Base backup plus WAL archiving for point-in-time recovery.

revisions.reason: Verified current PostgreSQL 18 documentation while keeping RPO/RTO business-owned.

practices.title: Prove restoration works
practices.statement: Restore into an isolated environment, verify critical behavior and permissions, time the exercise against RTO, and revise the runbook.

applicability.description: Systems that rely on backups for recovery.

authoritative_references.title: PostgreSQL continuous archiving and PITR
authoritative_references.supports: Recovery procedure mechanics; drill cadence remains risk-based.

revisions.reason: Retained restore testing but rejected a universal quarterly cadence.

practices.title: Enforce tenant isolation and resource boundaries
practices.statement: Centralize tenant data enforcement, test negative cross-tenant access, and bound tenant-heavy work to prevent noisy neighbors.

revisions.reason: Objective and high impact, but primary multitenancy authority is still required before catalog promotion.

practices.title: Establish a safe VPS baseline
practices.statement: Use non-root least privilege, verified key-based SSH, default-deny exposure, maintained updates, monitoring, tested recovery, and access runbooks before production.

revisions.reason: Verified current Ubuntu guidance; alternate SSH ports remain noise reduction, not a primary control.

practices.title: Treat managed hosting versus VPS as a contextual tradeoff
practices.statement: Compare workload, operational capacity, full cost, compliance, and migration paths rather than applying a universal hosting rule.

revisions.reason: Separated valid total-cost questions from promotional absolute claims.

practices.title: Measure time to first meaningful value
practices.statement: Define and instrument the smallest outcome proving core value, then test onboarding changes against that outcome and retained use.

applicability.description: End-user products with signup and onboarding.

revisions.reason: Retained outcome measurement and rejected a universal 60-second threshold.

practices.title: Review AI extensions as supply-chain code
practices.statement: Verify canonical sources and inspect install scripts, hooks, MCP servers, permissions, network calls, updates, licensing, and removal before adoption.

applicability.description: Projects adding third-party skills, plugins, agents, hooks, or MCP servers.

revisions.reason: Multiple clips expose the surface, but popularity and bundle recommendations do not establish safety.

practices.title: Distinguish local media processing from API transcription
practices.statement: Document whether captions, frames, video, or extracted audio leave the machine; local tooling does not imply an upload-free workflow when an API transcription backend is configured.

revisions.reason: Frame inspection and the Moviola security model distinguish local transforms from optional audio upload.

practices.title: Keep promotional claims out of audit failure criteria
practices.statement: Income, popularity, cost, speed, productivity multiplier, model-superlative, aesthetic, and product endorsement claims remain advisory until independently reproducible and relevant.

applicability.description: Any practice source containing promotional or subjective claims.

revisions.reason: Consolidated unverified claims so they can never silently become enforced rules.
